decision: Retain source unchanged; no concrete supported correction selected
selectedSemantics: Standalone entry/action/cancel and SortHeader controls are native buttons. No custom keyboard event emulation or universal inline Escape contract is established by this source.

Open path captures the actual row button and selected opaque ID. The stable PathDetail ref callback focuses its mounted h2 with tabIndex -1; the immediate parent focus attempt is not the sole entry mechanism.

Explicit Close path clears selection and focuses the connected row trigger, otherwise the path search input. Keyed row IDs survive sorting; a filtered or previous-page trigger may be disconnected and selects the existing fallback. No browser focus movement is proved.

Mount name and registration logical-path inputs use autoFocus. Explicit form close/success clears both forms and returns to its connected captured trigger or path search. Automatic permission-driven removal does not use closeForms; no universal focus-return guarantee is inferred.

MetadataTable starts with the first column ascending. useSort toggles the same key asc/desc and starts a new key ascending. SortHeader exposes its label and current direction in a native button accessible name; the parent th provides aria-sort. Actions have a separate nonsortable heading.

Mount revision, fieldCount, retention and version use numeric sort; createdAt uses date sort; other selected columns use natural text sort. compareValues places unknown values last in either direction. Equal column values use ascending id.localeCompare, including a descending primary sort; no locale-invariant order claim.

The table copies rows, sorts and renders at most100. Filtering/sort affect current permitted API-page metadata only. Selected detail and captured forms remain independent. No API reorder, server search, backend authorization, native value, version operation or request-contract change follows.

Parent entry wiring for administration and workbench remains explicit; this review reads boundary callbacks only and does not trace their private internals. Fresh administrator versus scoped-writer distinctions, ordinary failures/drafts and explicit mappings remain intact.
limitations: No React DOM/browser/keyboard/AT/backend acceptance; native button/default focus behavior is source wiring only
